claims.statement: The tracked root .env.example is the single configuration source shared by the backend, the Huey worker, Docker Compose interpolation and the frontend service; docker-compose.yml loads it via env_file for backend and worker, interpolates ports/URLs from it, and forwards VITE_* values plus JWT_SECRET to the frontend service.

docker-compose.yml derives the frontend SSR guard secret from the root .env by mapping SECRET_KEY to JWT_SECRET with a required-variable assertion, so frontend/src/hooks.server.ts verifies the auth_token cookie with the same HS256 key the backend signs with and no separate secret is configured.

Settings.model_config pins env_file to the literal ".env" relative to the working directory and uses extra="ignore", so stray files such as src/.env are ignored and unknown keys are tolerated; process environment variables override file values and defaults apply when no file exists.

Settings validates SECRET_KEY in an after-model validator: outside dev/test environments the key must be non-empty and at least MIN_SECRET_KEY_LENGTH = 32 characters or Settings() raises a ValidationError; dev and test may leave it empty.
Settings applies a before-field validator to smtp_sender_email that substitutes noreply@retail-portfolio.local when the configured value is missing or blank.

settings is a module-level Settings() singleton instantiated at import time, and consumers read it as an object (call-time attribute access) rather than re-instantiating Settings, which is why tests monkeypatch attributes on the singleton.

register_services in src/config/services.py is the single registration entry point for both the API and the worker: it registers the AsyncSession factory from the passed DatabaseSessionManager, registers core, account and auth services unconditionally, and then selects stub or live integration and market registrations based on settings.stub_external_api.

When settings.stub_external_api is true, register_integration_stub_services and register_market_stub_services replace the live factories for the same abstract keys, swapping WealthsimpleApiGateway for StubWealthsimpleApiGateway and AIService for StubAIService, so callers resolve identical keys with different implementations.

src/market/eodhd.py::eodhd_gateway_factory independently re-checks settings.stub_external_api and returns StubEodhdGateway instead of EodhdGateway, so the live market registration path still yields a stub gateway when stub mode is on; the registry-level and factory-level switches must stay consistent.

A new repository, service or domain API is only resolvable if it is registered in its domain's register_*_services function; the API process attaches the resulting registry to app.state.svcs_registry and route handlers receive a request-scoped svcs.fastapi.DepContainer for aget calls.

The Huey worker builds a second, independent registry in its on_startup handler using a fresh DatabaseSessionManager configured with NullPool, and stores it on huey.svcs_registry; NullPool avoids operation-in-progress errors when pooled async connections are reused across the per-task asyncio.run() event loops.

Huey task bodies resolve services through async with Container(huey.svcs_registry) after guarding for a missing registry: critical periodic tasks in src/market/task.py and src/account/task.py raise RuntimeError("Worker registry not initialized") while best-effort tasks such as _generate_note_title and _check_and_dispatch_price_alerts return early.

Task modules must import src.worker.huey and be imported by src/worker.py for their tasks to register with Huey; tests assert registration by looking up the qualified task name in huey._registry._registry.

DatabaseSessionManager owns one AsyncEngine and an async_sessionmaker(autocommit=False, expire_on_commit=False); session() rolls back on exception and always closes the session, connect() rolls back the connection on exception, and both raise SystemError if the manager was never initialized or has been closed.

A module-level sessionmanager is created from settings.database_url and settings.echo_sql and is imported directly by the API process, while the worker constructs its own NullPool instance from the same URL.
Alembic migrations run automatically at API startup through run_migrations(), which calls alembic.command.upgrade to head inside asyncio.to_thread; the step is skipped when environment is "test".

migrations/env.py imports each domain's model module so every table is registered on BaseModel.metadata before target_metadata is captured, derives target_metadata from src.config.database.BaseModel, and overrides sqlalchemy.url from the DATABASE_URL environment variable by rewriting postgresql+asyncpg:// to synchronous postgresql:// for the NullPool sync engine.

RedisManager keeps one redis.asyncio client per running event loop in a dictionary guarded by a threading.Lock: client() prunes and closes clients whose loop has closed, then lazily creates a decode_responses=True client for the current loop, which lets the single redis_manager singleton serve the request loop, the WebSocket listener and asyncio.run() task loops.

The redis_manager singleton is constructed from settings.redis_url and is the shared Redis access point for the auth token denylist, TOTP/passkey challenges, account sync status and the market security search cache; the WebSocket fan-out does not use it — src/ws/manager.py::ConnectionManager keeps its own per-event-loop client dict and src/ws/router.py opens a separate short-lived client for ticket replay checks — and IndicatorCache likewise builds its own client from settings.redis_url with decode_responses=False.

Tests never depend on a real Redis or vendor API: the autouse fake_redis_manager fixture replaces the shared redis_manager singleton's client (and the redis_manager aliases imported by src.auth.api and src.auth.service) with an in-memory FakeRedis, mock_redis_storage exposes the backing store, and tests/conftest.py sets STUB_EXTERNAL_API=true before importing the app.

The slowapi Limiter is module-level with headers_enabled=True, is attached as app.state.limiter with SlowAPIMiddleware and the rate-limit-exceeded handler, and uses memory:// storage when ENVIRONMENT or settings.environment is "test" and settings.redis_url otherwise, so the limit state is per-process in tests.

Rate limiting is keyed by user_or_ip_key_func, which decodes the auth_token cookie or Authorization header with settings.secret_key to return user:{user_id} from user_id or sub and otherwise falls back to the request's remote address, making the limit per authenticated user when a valid token is present.

Rate limits are applied per route with @limiter.limit decorators: 3/minute on the account import route and both integration connect routes, 5/minute on the auth login route and on the three AI market endpoints, and 10/minute on the remaining auth endpoints.

src/core/context.py exposes the request_id ContextVar through set_request_id (returning a reset token) and get_request_id, and Huey tasks reuse it by accepting a request_id argument, setting it, and resetting the token in a finally block so task logs inherit the originating request's correlation ID.

RequestIdMiddleware reuses an inbound X-Request-ID header or generates a UUID, stores it on request.state.request_id and the contextvar, logs one line per request with duration_ms at INFO or WARNING for 4xx, logs and re-raises on exception, echoes X-Request-ID on the response, and always resets the contextvar in a finally block.

init_logging() emits JSON logs via JsonFormatter and a RequestIdFilter when environment is "prod" (fields timestamp, level, logger, message, request_id plus optional user_id, domain, duration_ms, exc_info and stack_info), and otherwise uses a forced-terminal rich Console with a FallbackRichHandler that degrades to a stderr stream handler.

init_logging() calls logging.basicConfig(force=True), clears handlers on every existing logger and sets propagate=True so third-party loggers route through the root handler, quiets urllib3/httpx/watchfiles/faker/svcs/redis to INFO, and disables uvicorn.access because RequestIdMiddleware already logs each request.
Log level resolution in init_logging() prefers settings.log_level, then WARNING when environment is "test", then DEBUG.

settings.environment is the runtime mode switch consulted across the codebase: it enables debugpy in dev, sets FastAPI debug, adds a permissive origin regex and error-detail redaction outside prod, sets secure/httponly cookie flags in prod, selects MemoryHuey versus RedisHuey in test, and skips startup migrations in test.

The /health/ready endpoint resolves an AsyncSession from the svcs container, executes select(1), pings Redis through redis_manager.client(), and returns 200 when both report ok or 503 with status "degraded" otherwise.
The market document upload route reads settings.upload_path at request time, creates the directory with mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True), and writes each upload under a generated UUID filename.

Market, indicator and AI settings (eodhd_api_key, indicator_service_url, ai_api_endpoint, ai_api_key, ai_api_model) are read inside the corresponding factories rather than at import time, so a misconfigured value surfaces during service resolution or as a stubbed response.

Email delivery is configured from settings (smtp_host, smtp_port, smtp_use_tls, smtp_user, smtp_password, smtp_sender_email) and settings.frontend_url is used to build absolute verification links, price-alert deeplinks and external-account error deeplinks.

Auth security settings are read at call time: totp_max_attempts and totp_lockout_seconds gate the 2FA attempt counter and Redis lockout, and webauthn_rp_id, webauthn_rp_name, webauthn_origin and webauthn_challenge_ttl_seconds configure passkey registration and assertion.
settings.sync_ttl_seconds is applied as the TTL of the Redis set that tracks in-flight account syncs per user.

Settings defines the orchestrator subprocess URL and several remaining dev-stack defaults (frontend_url, database_url, cors_allow_origins, upload_path, redis_url, indicator_service_url, ai_api_endpoint) that mirror docker-compose.yml, so missing variables degrade to dev values instead of failing startup.

src/ws/manager.py::ConnectionManager (ws_manager) keeps its own Redis clients in a per-event-loop dict guarded by a threading lock; src/main.py initializes them in lifespan_context via ws_manager.init_redis(settings.redis_url), which also starts the listener subscribed to the ws_messages channel, and send_personal_message lazily initializes a client when the calling loop has none before publishing, falling back to local delivery when Redis is unreachable.

The account-sync status keys are written through redis_manager.client(): mark_sync_started SADDs the account id to account_syncs:active:{user_id} and applies EXPIRE settings.sync_ttl_seconds, mark_sync_finished SREMs it, and get_active_syncs returns the members parsed back into AccountId UUIDs, consumed by GET /api/v1/accounts/sync-status and the broker-sync task.

src/ws/router.py::_check_ticket_not_replayed does not use a shared Redis manager: it constructs a short-lived redis.asyncio client from settings.redis_url, performs SET NX EX 30 on ws-ticket-used:{sha256(ticket)}, and closes the client in a finally block.

WebSocket handlers reuse the app-lifetime registry rather than a request-scoped DepContainer: src/ws/router.py reads websocket.app.state.svcs_registry and opens its own svcs.Container to resolve UserApi for cookie/subprotocol token authentication.
register_core_services registers EmailService as a value (register_value(EmailService, EmailService())) rather than a factory, making it the one eagerly constructed service in the registry.

Only the market and integration domains branch on stub_external_api; core, account and auth services are registered identically in stub and live modes, as shown by the flow where account and auth registrations occur before the stub/live branch.
